correctness.rationale: For n>=m>=3 a chosen set of fewer than m vertices leaves a row and a column empty; at size m there is a full orientation with one chosen vertex per column (or its transposition on square boards). An occupied row must have >=2 chosen squares because selected vertices must have a selected neighbor. One-square exchanges preserve occupied columns and the entire occupied-row support: deleting a square from a two-occupied row is forbidden, while no target row can be previously empty. Within support r, bounded-fiber functions provide the exact graph H_{m,r}, with connected buffer transfers for m>=2r+1, no moves for m=2r, and a singleton for r=1. The correct 2-/3-subset inclusion graph at m=5 is the Desargues graph. Count by labeled surjections L_{m,r}=m![x^m](e^x-1-x)^r and source/destination directed moves E_{m,r}=binom(r,2)*m*L_{m-1,r}. Independent fresh enumerator compared actual open-neighborhood total domination and support function graph on six rectangular boards; 5x5 yielded 410 vertices, 600 edges, 10 isolates and 20 size-20 Desargues components. The finite checks corroborate the all-order combinatorial proof.

value.rationale: Minimum-total-domination reconfiguration is a natural reachability problem. The theorem gives every connected component across an infinite rook-graph family, a sharp spare-vertex threshold, exact edges and a canonical Desargues transition at five columns; this is not a restatement of the known total optimum-state count. Finite check complements an explicit all-order buffer construction.
